root_idea.summary: The root centers on play, sport, and activity lacking a straightforward serious purpose; it also has a distinct branch for saliva and flowing secretions.
root_idea.development: The lexical sources present play as action undertaken without a sound or purposeful objective, while Maqayis proposes the broader orientation of going without straightness. A separate established branch concerns saliva, plant mucilage, and analogous flowing or filmy substances.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the Quran-attested verbal noun.
Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form.

senses.definition: To play, sport, amuse oneself, or engage in activity without a serious or purposeful aim.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic Form I imperfect usage; the verb can describe ordinary play or frivolous activity contrasted with earnestness, without specifying a particular game.

senses.definition: Play, amusement, or diversion regarded as a non-serious activity rather than purposeful action.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic verbal-noun usage, including play or amusement contrasted with the purposeful reality of worldly or religious life.

senses.definition: One who plays, sports, or engages in frivolous amusement.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic active-participle usage; it can characterize people as engaged in play or as acting without earnest purpose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To toy, dally, flirt, or wanton with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional interpersonal use of the verb, including playful or amorous dalliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the wind, to obliterate or efface the traces of a dwelling or place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage applied to wind acting on visible traces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of waves, to toss people about without carrying them toward their intended destination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative description of the disorienting or unhelpful movement of waves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To salivate or drool; of a child, to emit a flow of saliva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct bodily-fluid sense of the verb, separate from play.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone play, or to bring someone something with which to play.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV construction; the supplied example uses a feminine object pronoun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To play repeatedly or time after time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intensive or repeated Form V usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm tree, to produce unripe dates or put forth a spadix retaining some of its first fruit after the earlier produce has been cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized botanical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who plays much or often; a habitual or great player.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive adjectival or nominal specialization, not the ordinary Quranic verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A turn in a game or play; a single act or round of playing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote one discrete occurrence or turn within a game.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular medicine resembling suranjan and said to promote fattening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Rare technical usage, distinct from the play-related noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing used for play, such as a game implement, toy, puppet, or effigy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes both game equipment and an image or figure made for play.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person with whom one plays or jokes; figuratively, a stupid person who becomes a laughing-stock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative personal use derived from treating someone as an object of amusement or ridicule.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The image seen in the black of the eye when an object faces it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized anatomical or optical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode, manner, or style of playing or sporting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the manner in which the activity is performed, not to a single turn or to an object used in play.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Saliva, slaver, or drivel flowing from the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary bodily-fluid noun; it may also describe accumulated saliva around the teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mucilage or a viscous secretion of plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plant-fluid usage related to the sense of a flowing secretion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The honey or sweet fluid of the date palm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized expression for a date-palm secretion or product.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A filmy substance seen in the air during intense midday heat, resembling cobwebs; by some accounts, a mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources distinguish this phenomenon from the ordinary midday mirage, while reporting both descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Playful, gamesome, or coquettishly flirtatious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive adjective used in the supplied expression for a woman who displays affected coyness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A player or gamer by profession or occupation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive occupational noun, indicating that playing is the person's business.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who takes another person's property as a prank in order to vex or anger its owner, without intending theft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A special use in which the action is playful with respect to theft but serious in its intention to annoy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing with which one plays, such as a toy or game implement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same form is also recorded as a verbal noun of لَعِبَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place for playing, sporting, gaming, or performing plays.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Can denote a physical venue or playing ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The courses or places where the wind blows or has blown vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative plural expression, equating the wind's courses with its playing places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bewildering place in which a person does not know where he is.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Idiomatic figurative expression, literally “the playing places of the jinn.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sleeveless garment in which a boy plays.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized clothing term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exuding mucilage; applied to a plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative botanical adjective likening the plant's secretion to a foolish person's dribbling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert bird noted for the swiftness with which it pounces down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Fixed bird-name expression, literally “one who plays with his shadow.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of teeth or front teeth, having saliva or drivel upon or around them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized passive-participial description of teeth affected by saliva.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Play, its verbal noun, and interpersonal dalliance are represented.
Illustrative single-game example covered by the turn sense.
Person treated as a plaything or laughing-stock represented.
Puppet or effigy is covered by the broader toy/object sense.
Manner or style of playing represented.
Frivolous or unprofitable action is covered by the Quranic active-participle sense.
Verbal-noun function is covered by the Quranic play noun.
Pointer-only list of forms referred to elsewhere.

cautions: The Quranic nominal group is presented as لَعِبٌ, while Lane also records related verbal-noun vocalizations such as لَعْبٌ and لِعْبٌ; those Classical variants are not additional Quranic form groups.
The Quranic active-participle group is morphologically reported by QAC as a nominal group but is normalized here to the singular citation form لَاعِبٌ.
